subject_model: Each case defines an AdaptationInput: {preferences, predictions, trials, sessionEvidence}. trials entries: {id, parameters, changedVariables, snapshots:[{freeNeutrons, absorbedNeutrons, escapedNeutrons, reactionEvents, cumulativeEnergyUnits, step}], startedAt, completedAt}. predictions: {id, trialId, prompt, answer, structuredAnswer, confidence, createdAt}. sessionEvidence: {representationEvents:[{mode, openedAt}], adaptationProposals:[{id, type, decision, evidenceIds, reason, createdAt}], conceptEvidence:[{conceptId, status, evidenceIds}]}. expected_proposals: types that MUST be proposed. forbidden_proposals: types that MUST NOT be proposed. abstention_expected: true means zero proposals expected. required_evidence_ids: ids that must appear in the evidenceIds of every produced proposal. Rule order in the implementation: ask_prediction_again, freeze_variables, show_graph, compare_trials, slow_animation, show_causal_view, reduce_density; max 3 proposals; rejected types are never re-proposed.

cases.title: Learner requests less text: reduce_density must not fire redundantly

predictions.answer: It gets slightly faster

cases.notes: KNOWN DEFECT: the rule fires reduce_density on any ceiling-hit trial when no proposal was accepted yet — it does not check the CURRENT informationDensity (deterministic-provider.ts:180-193). Proposing 'less text' to a learner who already set low density is a generic-feeling misfire. Fix: skip when informationDensity is already 'low' or learner chose 'full' (~0.5h).

cases.title: Immediate feedback disabled: feedbackTiming must change behavior

predictions.answer: It gets slightly faster

cases.notes: feedbackTiming is settable and persisted but consumed by NO code path (learner.ts:38,56,70; accessibility-controls.tsx:115-134). The same proposals fire regardless of the setting. Either wire it (delay/limit adaptation-card display timing) or remove the control (2-6h).

cases.title: Corrupt session event: provider must not throw

predictions.answer: It grows much faster than before

cases.notes: Malformed evidence must not crash the provider; the zod schema at the storage boundary would reject this on load (session-storage.ts:51-66) and the provider itself only reads fields it needs. Expected outcome: graceful abstention.

cases.title: Repeated identical proposal: identical inputs yield identical rule selections

predictions.answer: It gets slightly faster

cases.notes: Calling propose() twice with this exact input must yield the same two types in the same order (determinism contract, tested). Proposal UUIDs may differ; rule selection must not.

cases.title: Adaptation must never change multiple counterfactual variables

predictions.answer: It grows much faster than before

cases.notes: runCounterfactual takes exactly ONE variable from the allowlist and throws for anything else; seed and durationSteps are excluded (counterfactual.ts:15-42). The counterfactual panel exposes a single-variable select. Multi-variable counterfactuals are structurally impossible.
